summary: EU-WEST Dedicated escalation: repeated TP hangs/timeouts under sustained streaming load; request hotfix build + coordinated traffic shift mitigation
description:
Issue summary
- Customer (HelioDesk, Dedicated, eu-west) reporting repeated request hangs/timeouts during tensor-parallel (TP) workloads. Impact is concentrated during sustained high concurrency with long-running streaming responses.
- Customer escalation asks for (1) immediate mitigation to stop hangs today, and (2) a hotfix build they can deploy to their Dedicated cluster without waiting for full runtime release.

Impact
- Customer observed: intermittent streaming responses that never complete, followed by client-side timeouts. Once the issue starts, a subset of traffic continues failing until pool is drained/restarted.
- Customer-facing symptom: elevated 5xx/timeouts on chat completion endpoints; degraded SLO for end-users.
- Redwood impact: repeated oncall engagement + manual mitigations.

Customer context
- Deployment: Dedicated GPU pool in eu-west.
- Workload: high concurrency chat + long outputs (streaming), mixed sequence lengths.
- Models: llama-3-70b-instruct (primary), qwen2.5-72b-instruct (secondary).

Timeline (customer-reported)
- 2025-02-27 ~18:40 UTC: first spike in hangs; temporary relief after restarting a subset of runtime pods.
- 2025-02-28 08:10 UTC: recurrence; customer escalated requesting hotfix.

What we see (Redwood side)
- Pattern matches known TP hang signatures under load (suspected: cancellation/barrier deadlock + delayed async error propagation in collectives).
- Cluster enters partial forward-progress stall: some TP groups stop making progress, but remain “healthy” from scheduler perspective and continue receiving work.

Indicators / evidence
- Customer logs (redacted) indicate long gaps with no token progress while streams remain open.
- Redwood side signals during incidents (eu-west Dedicated):
  - Increased p99 stream duration without corresponding token throughput.
  - Burst of request cancels/timeouts correlating with collective latency spikes.

Selected log snippets (from Redwood runtime, eu-west)
- 2025-02-28T07:58:31Z level=ERROR component=collectives msg="nccl allreduce stalled" tp_group_id=tp-7b2c rank=3 op=allreduce bytes=1048576 elapsed_ms=61234 stream=comm
- 2025-02-28T07:58:32Z level=WARN component=scheduler msg="no forward progress" tp_group_id=tp-7b2c inflight_requests=28 last_progress_ms_ago=61500 state=RUNNING
- 2025-02-28T07:59:10Z level=INFO component=request msg="cancellation received" request_id=req_01H... reason=client_disconnect streaming=true
- 2025-02-28T07:59:10Z level=WARN component=scheduler msg="barrier wait exceeded" tp_group_id=tp-7b2c barrier=decode_step elapsed_ms=30000 pending_ranks=1

Immediate mitigation requested
- Shift traffic away from affected pool / drain stuck TP groups.
- Provide recommended config knobs (timeout thresholds / disable TP / reduce concurrency) for short-term stability.

Hotfix request
- Customer asks for a hotfix build containing TP hang mitigations (cancellation-safe barriers + collective async error checks + TP-group watchdog/quarantine) for eu-west Dedicated.

Actions / ownership
- Support (Dev Patel / Owen Phillips): customer comms + coordination.
- SRE (Rafael Mendes): traffic shift/drain plan, safety gates, monitoring.
- Runtime Eng (Sofia Ivanova / Hiro Tanaka): confirm fix set for hotfix and provide build artifact.

Proposed plan
1) Stop the bleeding (today)
- Drain/quarantine suspected stuck TP groups by draining runtime pods and shifting capacity.
- Temporary config: reduce max concurrent streams per TP group; prefer shorter max_output_tokens; increase request timeout on client only if needed (avoid hiding stalls).
2) Hotfix build for Dedicated
- Candidate patch set: PR-18441 (cancellation/barrier), PR-18455 (async error checks), PR-18462 (watchdog/quarantine), PR-18473 (tuning knobs).
- Rollout: staged to a subset of HelioDesk pool, then expand.

Customer-facing notes / limitations (for comms)
- We can mitigate symptoms today via traffic shifting/draining and throttling.
- Full resolution expected after hotfix deploy; we’ll ask customer to run a controlled load test and report if any “silent stalls” persist.

Next update SLA
- Provide mitigation status within 2 hours.
- Provide hotfix build ETA once runtime confirms patch selection and release gating.
comments:
2025-02-28 08:22 UTC — Dev Patel (Reporter)
Escalation from HelioDesk (Dedicated, eu-west): they’re seeing repeated hangs during streaming at high concurrency. They’re asking for a hotfix build; they can’t wait for the next standard runtime release. Tagging SRE + runtime eng. Customer notes the issue is worse when clients disconnect mid-stream.

Customer asks:
1) Immediate mitigation to stop ongoing timeouts.
2) Hotfix build they can deploy to their Dedicated pool.

Attaching customer’s redacted timestamps + request IDs in the internal case notes.

2025-02-28 08:35 UTC — Owen Phillips (Assignee)
Acknowledged. I’ll own comms cadence + incident coordination.

Looping in Rafael Mendes for traffic shift options and Sofia Ivanova/Hiro Tanaka for hotfix feasibility.

Initial guidance to customer (pending): temporarily reduce concurrency + keep-alive, and avoid aggressive client disconnects while we mitigate.

2025-02-28 08:49 UTC — Rafael Mendes (SRE)
Checked eu-west Dedicated dashboards: spikes in request timeouts correlate with collective latency increase on a subset of hosts.

Immediate mitigation proposal:
- Shift ~40% traffic to HelioDesk secondary pool (eu-central) if available; otherwise temporarily burst to Hosted fallback in eu-central (if contract allows) while we drain eu-west.
- Drain runtime pods on suspected stuck hosts; mark nodes for investigation.

I can execute a controlled drain within 30 minutes if Support confirms with customer (short maintenance window).

2025-02-28 09:03 UTC — Owen Phillips (Support)
Sent customer an update proposing a 20–30 min maintenance window to drain affected pods and shift traffic. Waiting on approval.

Requested from customer:
- Approx QPS, max_output_tokens distribution
- Whether they can temporarily cap concurrency and enforce server-side request timeouts
- Confirmation whether eu-central pool is enabled for them

2025-02-28 09:18 UTC — Sofia Ivanova (Runtime Scheduling)
This matches the cancellation/barrier deadlock we’ve been chasing (see SUP-9827). PR-18441 should address the deadlock path when a request is canceled mid-decode and one rank lags at the barrier.

For hotfix: we strongly prefer bundling watchdog/quarantine (PR-18462) so stuck TP groups stop receiving work and self-heal (controlled teardown). Otherwise you can still end up with “zombie” groups.

We need to confirm risk for Dedicated patch release and finalize thresholds for eu-west workloads.

2025-02-28 09:27 UTC — Hiro Tanaka (Runtime Kernels)
From kernel/collectives side: PR-18455 adds periodic async error checks for NCCL collectives and surfaces failures to scheduler instead of silent stalls.

If customer is seeing “hangs with no errors”, this is likely contributing. I recommend including PR-18455 in the hotfix.

We’ll provide a candidate build once release coord approves; want perf sanity pass to ensure no throughput regression.

2025-02-28 09:41 UTC — Rafael Mendes (SRE)
Customer approved maintenance window.

Action taken:
- 09:35–09:40 UTC: drained 12 runtime pods across 3 nodes showing stalled collectives.
- Shifted 35% of traffic to eu-central fallback capacity (temporary).

Current state (09:41 UTC): timeout rate dropping; still monitoring for recurrence.

Please tell customer: we expect stability improved immediately, but underlying bug still possible under sustained load until hotfix.

2025-02-28 10:02 UTC — Owen Phillips (Support)
Updated customer: mitigation in place (drain + partial traffic shift). Asked them to run a controlled load test and confirm whether hangs recur.

Customer asks again for hotfix ETA. They can accept a staged rollout next week, but want a build early next week at the latest.

2025-02-28 11:10 UTC — Connor O'Brien (Releases)
We can cut a Dedicated-only hotfix if we keep scope tight and have rollback gates.

Requirements:
- Identify exact PR SHAs: 18441, 18455, 18462, 18473
- SRE to define rollback trigger thresholds (watchdog false positives, reset loop, p99 latency regression)
- Customer to accept canary on 10% of pool for 2–4 hours before full rollout

If runtime confirms today, we can target build artifact by Monday EOD (eu-west time).

2025-03-03 16:24 UTC — Sofia Ivanova (Runtime Scheduling)
Hotfix candidate branch prepared (runtime 1.19.1-hotfix.2). Includes:
- PR-18441 cancellation-safe barrier logic
- PR-18462 TP-group watchdog + quarantine
- PR-18473 config knobs to tune watchdog sensitivity

Default thresholds are conservative; for HelioDesk we’ll set:
- watchdog_no_progress_ms=45000
- collective_warn_ms=20000
- quarantine_cooldown_s=120

Need SRE signoff on thresholds and Support signoff with customer re: expected behavior (quarantine triggers will reset groups; may cause brief blips but prevents long hangs).

2025-03-04 09:05 UTC — Rafael Mendes (SRE)
Deployed hotfix to 2/20 nodes (10% canary) in HelioDesk eu-west Dedicated pool.

Observed (first 90 min):
- No stuck streams.
- 2 watchdog triggers due to induced load spike; both recovered within ~35s and did not cascade.
- p99 latency +2.1% vs baseline during canary window; within acceptable range.

Proceeding to expand to 50% pending customer confirmation.

2025-03-04 11:22 UTC — Owen Phillips (Support)
Customer confirms: since canary started, no hanging streams; they did notice two brief blips consistent with resets, but prefer that over multi-minute hangs.

Approved expanding rollout. Requested written summary for their incident report (what happened, what we changed, what remains).

2025-03-05 08:40 UTC — Rafael Mendes (SRE)
Rollout complete to 100% of HelioDesk eu-west pool.

Last 12h:
- Timeouts back to baseline.
- Watchdog triggers: 3 total (auto-recovered) and no sustained stalls.

We’ll keep eu-central traffic shift in place at 10% for another 24h as a safety valve, then return to normal routing if stable.

2025-03-05 15:10 UTC — Dev Patel (Support escalation)
Sent customer summary + next steps:
- Root cause suspected: TP-group deadlock on cancellation + delayed collective error surfacing.
- Mitigation: drained affected nodes and temporarily shifted traffic.
- Fix: dedicated hotfix build enabling cancellation-safe barriers + collective async error checks + TP-group watchdog/quarantine.

Customer asks to stay on hotfix until official runtime release. I told them we’ll align on standard runtime 1.19.x once GA, with a planned maintenance window.

2025-03-06 10:55 UTC — Owen Phillips (Support)
Closing as resolved.

Resolution
- Immediate mitigation: traffic shift + draining stuck nodes.
- Permanent mitigation for customer: runtime 1.19.1-hotfix deployed to Dedicated eu-west pool with watchdog/quarantine enabled and tuned thresholds.

Follow-ups
- Link this case to ongoing TP stability initiative and ensure standard release notes mention behavior change (quarantine resets instead of silent hangs).
- Keep INT-611 open for alerting improvements in eu-west Dedicated (watchdog trigger rate + collective latency).
